sanskrit_shloka:
पञ्चानामपि कोशानामपवादे विभात्ययं शुद्धः ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसः प्रत्यग्रूपः परः स्वयंज्योतिः ॥ १५१ ॥
transliteration:
pañcānāmapi kośānāmapavāde vibhātyayaṃ śuddhaḥ |
nityānandaikarasaḥ pratyagrūpaḥ paraḥ svayaṃjyotiḥ || 151 ||
translation: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated, the Self of man appears – pure, of the essence of everlasting and unalloyed bliss, indwelling, supreme and self-effulgent.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When all the five sheaths have been eliminated, the Self of man appears – pure, of the essence of everlasting and unalloyed bliss, indwelling, supreme and self-effulgent.

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मानात्मविवेकः कर्तव्यो बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ।
तेनैवानन्दी भवति स्वं विज्ञाय सच्चिदानन्दम् ॥ १५२ ॥
transliteration:
ātmānātmavivekaḥ kartavyo bandhamuktaye viduṣā |
tenaivānandī bhavati svaṃ vijñāya saccidānandam || 152 ||
translation: To remove his bondage the wise man should discriminate between the Self and the non-Self. By that alone he comes to know his own Self as Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute and becomes happy.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To remove his bondage the wise man should discriminate between the Self and the non-Self. By that alone he comes to know his own Self as Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute and becomes happy.

sanskrit_shloka:
मुञ्जादिषीकामिव दृश्यवर्गात् प्रत्यञ्चमात्मानमसङ्गमक्रियम् ।
विविच्य तत्र प्रविलाप्य सर्वं तदात्मना तिष्ठति यः स मुक्तः ॥ १५३ ॥
transliteration:
muñjādiṣīkāmiva dṛśyavargāt pratyañcamātmānamasaṅgamakriyam |
vivicya tatra pravilāpya sarvaṃ tadātmanā tiṣṭhati yaḥ sa muktaḥ || 153 ||
translation: He indeed is free who discriminates between all sense-objects and the indwelling, unattached and inactive Self – as one separates a stalk of grass from its enveloping sheath – and merging everything in It, remains in a state of identity with That.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He indeed is free who discriminates between all sense-objects and the indwelling, unattached and inactive Self – as one separates a stalk of grass from its enveloping sheath – and merging everything in It, remains in a state of identity with That.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहोऽयमन्नभवनोऽन्नमायास्तु कोशः चान्नेन जीवति विनश्यति तद्विहीनः ।
त्वक्चर्ममांसरुधिरास्थिपुरीषराशिः नायं स्वयं भवितुमर्हति नित्यशुद्धः ॥ १५४ ॥
transliteration:
deho'yamannabhavano'nnaMāyāstu kośaḥ cānnena jīvati vinaśyati tadvihīnaḥ |
tvakcarmamāṃsarudhirāsthipurīṣarāśiḥ nāyaṃ svayaṃ bhavitumarhati nityaśuddhaḥ || 154 ||
translation: This body of ours is the product of food and comprises the material sheath; it lives on food and dies without it; it is a mass of skin, flesh, blood, bones and filth, and can never be the eternally pure, self-existent Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This body of ours is the product of food and comprises the material sheath; it lives on food and dies without it; it is a mass of skin, flesh, blood, bones and filth, and can never be the eternally pure, self-existent Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
पूर्वं जनेरधिमृतेरपि नायमस्ति जातक्षणः क्षणगुणोऽनियतस्वभावः ।
नैको जडश्च घटवत्परिदृश्यमानः स्वात्मा कथं भवति भावविकारवेत्ता ॥ १५५ ॥
transliteration:
pūrvaṃ janeradhimṛterapi nāyamasti jātakṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇaguṇo'niyatasvabhāvaḥ |
naiko jaḍaśca ghaṭavatparidṛśyamānaḥ svātmā kathaṃ bhavati bhāvavikāravettā || 155 ||
translation: It does not exist prior to inception or posterior to dissolution, but lasts only for a short (intervening) period; its virtues are transient, and it is changeful by nature; it is manifold, inert, and is a sense-object, like a jar; how can it be one’s own Self, the Witness of changes in all things?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It does not exist prior to inception or posterior to dissolution, but lasts only for a short (intervening) period; its virtues are transient, and it is changeful by nature; it is manifold, inert, and is a sense-object, like a jar; how can it be one’s own Self, the Witness of changes in all things?

sanskrit_shloka:
पाणिपादादिमान्देहो नात्मा व्यङ्गेऽपि जीवनात् ।
तत्तच्छक्तेरनाशाच्च न नियम्यो नियामकः ॥ १५६ ॥
transliteration:
pāṇipādādimāndeho nātmā vyaṅge'pi jīvanāt |
tattacchakteranāśācca na niyamyo niyāmakaḥ || 156 ||
translation: The body, consisting of arms, legs, etc., cannot be the Ātman, for one continues to live even when particular limbs are gone, and the different functions of the organism also remain intact. The body which is subject to another’s rule cannot be the Self which is the Ruler of all.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The body, consisting of arms, legs, etc., cannot be the Ātman, for one continues to live even when particular limbs are gone, and the different functions of the organism also remain intact. The body which is subject to another’s rule cannot be the Self which is the Ruler of all.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहतद्धर्मतत्कर्मतदवस्थादिसाक्षिणः ।
सत एव स्वतःसिद्धं तद्वैलक्षण्यमात्मनः ॥ १५७ ॥
transliteration:
dehataddharmatatkarmatadavasthādisākṣiṇaḥ |
sata eva svataḥsiddhaṃ tadvailakṣaṇyamātmanaḥ || 157 ||
translation: That the Ātman as the abiding Reality is different from the body, its characteristics, its activities, its states, etc., of which It is the witness, is self-evident.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That the Ātman as the abiding Reality is different from the body, its characteristics, its activities, its states, etc., of which It is the witness, is self-evident.

sanskrit_shloka:
शल्यराशिर्मांसलिप्तो मलपूर्णोऽतिकश्मलः ।
कथं भवेदयं वेत्ता स्वयमेतद्विलक्षणः ॥ १५८ ॥
transliteration:
śalyarāśirmāṃsalipto malapūrṇo'tikaśmalaḥ |
kathaṃ bhavedayaṃ vettā svayametadvilakṣaṇaḥ || 158 ||
translation: How can the body, being a pack of bones, covered with flesh, full of filth and highly impure, be the self-existent Ātman, the Knower, which is ever distinct from it?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How can the body, being a pack of bones, covered with flesh, full of filth and highly impure, be the self-existent Ātman, the Knower, which is ever distinct from it?

sanskrit_shloka:
त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशा वहंमतिं मूढजनः करोति ।
विलक्षणं वेत्ति विचारशीलो निजस्वरूपं परमार्थ भूतम् ॥ १५९ ॥
transliteration:
tvaṅmāṃsamedo'sthipurīṣarāśā vahaṃmatiṃ mūḍhajanaḥ karoti |
vilakṣaṇaṃ vetti vicāraśīlo nijasvarūpaṃ paramārtha bhūtam || 159 ||
translation: It is the foolish man who identifies himself with a mass of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, while the man of discrimination knows his own Self, the only Reality that there is, as distinct from the body.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is the foolish man who identifies himself with a mass of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, while the man of discrimination knows his own Self, the only Reality that there is, as distinct from the body.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहोऽहमित्येव जडस्य बुद्धिः देहे च जीवे विदुषस्त्वहंधीः ।
विवेकविज्ञानवतो महात्मनो ब्रह्माहमित्येव मतिः सदात्मनि ॥ १६0 ॥
transliteration:
deho'hamityeva jaḍasya buddhiḥ dehe ca jīve viduṣastvahaṃdhīḥ |
vivekavijñānavato mahātmano brahmāhamityeva matiḥ sadātmani || 160 ||
translation: The stupid man thinks he is the body, the book-learned man identifies himself with the mixture of body and soul, while the sage possessed of realisation due to discrimination looks upon the eternal Ātman as his Self, and thinks, 'I am Brahman'.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The stupid man thinks he is the body, the book-learned man identifies himself with the mixture of body and soul, while the sage possessed of realisation due to discrimination looks upon the eternal Ātman as his Self, and thinks, 'I am Brahman'.

sanskrit_shloka:
अत्रात्मबुद्धिं त्यज मूढबुद्धे त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशौ ।
सर्वात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे कुरुष्व शान्ति परमां भजस्व ॥ १६१ ॥
transliteration:
atrātmabuddhiṃ tyaja mūḍhabuddhe tvaṅmāṃsamedo'sthipurīṣarāśau |
sarvātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe kuruṣva śānti paramāṃ bhajasva || 161 ||
translation: O foolish person, cease to identify thyself with this bundle of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, and identify thyself instead with the Absolute Brahman, the Self of all, and thus attain to supreme Peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: O foolish person, cease to identify thyself with this bundle of skin, flesh, fat, bones and filth, and identify thyself instead with the Absolute Brahman, the Self of all, and thus attain to supreme Peace.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहेन्द्रियादावसति भ्रमोदितां विद्वानहं तां न जहाति यावत् ।
तावन्न तस्यास्ति विमुक्तिवार्ताप्य् अस्त्वेष वेदान्तनयान्तदर्शी ॥ १६२ ॥
transliteration:
dehendriyādāvasati bhramoditāṃ vidvānahaṃ tāṃ na jahāti yāvat |
tāvanna tasyāsti vimuktivārtāpy astveṣa vedāntanayāntadarśī || 162 ||
translation: As long as the book-learned man does not give up his mistaken identification with the body, organs, etc., which are unreal, there is no talk of emancipation for him, even if he be ever so erudite in the Vedanta philosophy.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As long as the book-learned man does not give up his mistaken identification with the body, organs, etc., which are unreal, there is no talk of emancipation for him, even if he be ever so erudite in the Vedanta philosophy.

sanskrit_shloka:
छायाशरीरे प्रतिबिम्बगात्रे यत्स्वप्नदेहे हृदि कल्पिताङ्गे ।
यथात्मबुद्धिस्तव नास्ति काचिज् जीवच्छरीरे च तथैव मास्तु ॥ १६३ ॥
transliteration:
chāyāśarīre pratibimbagātre yatsvapnadehe hṛdi kalpitāṅge |
yathātmabuddhistava nāsti kācij jīvaccharīre ca tathaiva māstu || 163 ||
translation: Just as thou dost not identify thyself with the shadow-body, the image-body, the dream-body, or the body thou hast in the imaginations of thy heart, cease thou to do likewise with the living body also.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as thou dost not identify thyself with the shadow-body, the image-body, the dream-body, or the body thou hast in the imaginations of thy heart, cease thou to do likewise with the living body also.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहात्मधीरेव नृणामसद्धियां जन्मादिदुःखप्रभवस्य बीजम् ।
यतस्ततस्त्वं जहि तां प्रयत्नात् त्यक्ते तु चित्ते न पुनर्भवाशा ॥ १६४ ॥
transliteration:
dehātmadhīreva nṛṇāmasaddhiyāṃ janmādiduḥkhaprabhavasya bījam |
yatastatastvaṃ jahi tāṃ prayatnāt tyakte tu citte na punarbhavāśā || 164 ||
translation: Identifications with the body alone is the root that produces the misery of birth etc., of people who are attached to the unreal; therefore destroy thou this with the utmost care. When this identification caused by the mind is given up, there is no more chance for rebirth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Identifications with the body alone is the root that produces the misery of birth etc., of people who are attached to the unreal; therefore destroy thou this with the utmost care. When this identification caused by the mind is given up, there is no more chance for rebirth.

sanskrit_shloka:
कर्मेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिरञ्चितोऽयं प्राणो भवेत्प्राणमायास्तु कोशः ।
येनात्मवानन्नमयोऽनुपूर्णः प्रवर्ततेऽसौ सकलक्रियासु ॥ १६५ ॥
transliteration:
karmendriyaiḥ pañcabhirañcito'yaṃ prāṇo bhavetprāṇaMāyāstu kośaḥ |
yenātmavānannamayo'nupūrṇaḥ pravartate'sau sakalakriyāsu || 165 ||
translation: The Prāṇa, with which we are all familiar, coupled with the five organs of action, forms the vital sheath, permeated by which the material sheath engages itself in all activities as if it were living.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Prāṇa, with which we are all familiar, coupled with the five organs of action, forms the vital sheath, permeated by which the material sheath engages itself in all activities as if it were living.

sanskrit_shloka:
नैवात्मापि प्राणमयो वायुविकारो गन्तागन्ता वायुवदन्तर्बहिरेषः ।
यस्मात्किंचित्क्वापि न वेत्तीष्टमनिष्टं स्वं वान्यं वा किंचन नित्यं परतन्त्रः ॥ १६६ ॥
transliteration:
naivātmāpi prāṇamayo vāyuvikāro gantāgantā vāyuvadantarbahireṣaḥ |
yasmātkiṃcitkvāpi na vettīṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ svaṃ vānyaṃ vā kiṃcana nityaṃ paratantraḥ || 166 ||
translation: Neither is the vital sheath the Self – because it is a modification of Vayu, and like the air it enters into and comes out of the body, and because it never knows in the least either its own weal and woe or those of others, being eternally dependent on the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Neither is the vital sheath the Self – because it is a modification of Vayu, and like the air it enters into and comes out of the body, and because it never knows in the least either its own weal and woe or those of others, being eternally dependent on the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि च मनश्च मनोमायाः स्यात् कोशो ममाहमिति वस्तुविकल्पहेतुः ।
संज्ञादिभेदकलनाकलितो बलीयांस् तत्पूर्वकोशमभिपूर्य विजृम्भते यः ॥ १६७ ॥
transliteration:
jñānendriyāṇi ca manaśca manoMāyāḥ syāt kośo mamāhamiti vastuvikalpahetuḥ |
saṃjñādibhedakalanākalito balīyāṃs tatpūrvakośamabhipūrya vijṛmbhate yaḥ || 167 ||
translation: The organs of knowledge together with the mind form the mental sheath – the cause of the diversity of things such as 'I' and 'mine'. It is powerful and endued with the faculty of creating differences of name etc., It manifests itself as permeating the preceding, i.e. the vital sheath.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The organs of knowledge together with the mind form the mental sheath – the cause of the diversity of things such as 'I' and 'mine'. It is powerful and endued with the faculty of creating differences of name etc., It manifests itself as permeating the preceding, i.e. the vital sheath.

sanskrit_shloka:
पञ्चेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिरेव होतृभिः प्रचीयमानो विषयाज्यधारया ।
जाज्वल्यमानो बहुवासनेन्धनैः मनोमयाग्निर्दहति प्रपञ्चम् ॥ १६८ ॥
transliteration:
pañcendriyaiḥ pañcabhireva hotṛbhiḥ pracīyamāno viṣayājyadhārayā |
jājvalyamāno bahuvāsanendhanaiḥ manomayāgnirdahati prapañcam || 168 ||
translation: The mental sheath is the (sacrificial) fire which, fed with the fuel of numerous desires by the five sense-organs which serve as priests, and set ablaze by the sense- objects which act as the stream of oblations, brings about this phenomenal universe.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The mental sheath is the (sacrificial) fire which, fed with the fuel of numerous desires by the five sense-organs which serve as priests, and set ablaze by the sense- objects which act as the stream of oblations, brings about this phenomenal universe.

sanskrit_shloka:
न ह्यस्त्यविद्या मनसोऽतिरिक्ता मनो ह्यविद्या भवबन्धहेतुः ।
तस्मिन्विनष्टे सकलं विनष्टं विजृम्भितेऽस्मिन्सकलं विजृम्भते ॥ १६९ ॥
transliteration:
na hyastyavidyā manaso'tiriktā mano hyavidyā bhavabandhahetuḥ |
tasminvinaṣṭe sakalaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ vijṛmbhite'sminsakalaṃ vijṛmbhate || 169 ||
translation: There is no Ignorance (Avidya) outside the mind. The mind alone is Avidya, the cause of the bondage of transmigration. When that is destroyed, all else is destroyed, and when it is manifested, everything else is manifested.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is no Ignorance (Avidya) outside the mind. The mind alone is Avidya, the cause of the bondage of transmigration. When that is destroyed, all else is destroyed, and when it is manifested, everything else is manifested.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वप्नेऽर्थशून्ये सृजति स्वशक्त्या भोक्त्रादिविश्वं मन एव सर्वम् ।
तथैव जाग्रत्यपि नो विशेषः तत्सर्वमेतन्मनसो विजृम्भणम् ॥ १७0 ॥
transliteration:
svapne'rthaśūnye sṛjati svaśaktyā bhoktrādiviśvaṃ mana eva sarvam |
tathaiva jāgratyapi no viśeṣaḥ tatsarvametanmanaso vijṛmbhaṇam || 170 ||
translation: In dreams, when there is no actual contact with the external world, the mind alone creates the whole universe consisting of the experiencer etc. Similarly in the waking state also; there is no difference. Therefore all this (phenomenal universe) is the projection of the mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In dreams, when there is no actual contact with the external world, the mind alone creates the whole universe consisting of the experiencer etc. Similarly in the waking state also; there is no difference. Therefore all this (phenomenal universe) is the projection of the mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
सुषुप्तिकाले मनसि प्रलीने नैवास्ति किंचित्सकलप्रसिद्धेः ।
अतो मनःकल्पितेव पुंसः संसार एतस्य न वस्तुतोऽस्ति ॥ १७१ ॥
transliteration:
suṣuptikāle manasi pralīne naivāsti kiṃcitsakalaprasiddheḥ |
ato manaḥkalpiteva puṃsaḥ saṃsāra etasya na vastuto'sti || 171 ||
translation: In dreamless sleep, when the mind is reduced to its causal state, there exists nothing (for the person asleep), as is evident from universal experience. Hence man’s relative existence is simply the creation of his mind, and has no objective reality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In dreamless sleep, when the mind is reduced to its causal state, there exists nothing (for the person asleep), as is evident from universal experience. Hence man’s relative existence is simply the creation of his mind, and has no objective reality.

sanskrit_shloka:
वायुनानीयते मेधः पुनस्तेनैव नीयते ।
मनसा कल्प्यते बन्धो मोक्षस्तेनैव कल्प्यते ॥ १७२ ॥
transliteration:
vāyunānīyate medhaḥ punastenaiva nīyate |
manasā kalpyate bandho mokṣastenaiva kalpyate || 172 ||
translation: Clouds are brought in by the wind and again driven away by the same agency. Similarly, man’s bondage is caused by the mind, and Liberation too is caused by that alone.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Clouds are brought in by the wind and again driven away by the same agency. Similarly, man’s bondage is caused by the mind, and Liberation too is caused by that alone.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहादिसर्वविषये परिकल्प्य रागं बध्नाति तेन पुरुषं पशुवद्गुणेन ।
वैरस्यमत्र विषवत्सुवुधाय पश्चाद् एनं विमोचयति तन्मन एव बन्धात् ॥ १७३ ॥
transliteration:
dehādisarvaviṣaye parikalpya rāgaṃ badhnāti tena puruṣaṃ paśuvadguṇena |
vairasyamatra viṣavatsuvudhāya paścād enaṃ vimocayati tanmana eva bandhāt || 173 ||
translation: It (first) creates an attachment in man for the body and all other sense-objects, and binds him through that attachment like a beast by means of ropes. Afterwards, the selfsame mind creates in the individual an utter distaste for these sense-objects as if they were poison, and frees him from the bondage.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It (first) creates an attachment in man for the body and all other sense-objects, and binds him through that attachment like a beast by means of ropes. Afterwards, the selfsame mind creates in the individual an utter distaste for these sense-objects as if they were poison, and frees him from the bondage.

sanskrit_shloka:
तस्मान्मनः कारणमस्य जन्तोः बन्धस्य मोक्षस्य च वा विधाने ।
बन्धस्य हेतुर्मलिनं रजोगुणैः मोक्षस्य शुद्धं विरजस्तमस्कम् ॥ १७४ ॥
transliteration:
tasmānmanaḥ kāraṇamasya jantoḥ bandhasya mokṣasya ca vā vidhāne |
bandhasya heturmalinaṃ rajoguṇaiḥ mokṣasya śuddhaṃ virajastamaskam || 174 ||
translation: Therefore the mind is the only cause that brings about man’s bondage or Liberation: when tainted by the effects of Rajas it leads to bondage, and when pure and divested of the Rajas and Tamas elements it conduces to Liberation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore the mind is the only cause that brings about man’s bondage or Liberation: when tainted by the effects of Rajas it leads to bondage, and when pure and divested of the Rajas and Tamas elements it conduces to Liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
विवेकवैराग्यगुणातिरेकाच् छुद्धत्वमासाद्य मनो विमुक्त्यै ।
भवत्यतो बुद्धिमतो मुमुक्षोस् ताभ्यां दृढाभ्यां भवितव्यमग्रे ॥ १७५ ॥
transliteration:
vivekavairāgyaguṇātirekāc chuddhatvamāsādya mano vimuktyai |
bhavatyato buddhimato mumukṣos tābhyāṃ dṛḍhābhyāṃ bhavitavyamagre || 175 ||
translation: Attaining purity through a preponderance of discrimination and renunciation, the mind makes for Liberation. Hence the wise seeker after Liberation must first strengthen these two.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Attaining purity through a preponderance of discrimination and renunciation, the mind makes for Liberation. Hence the wise seeker after Liberation must first strengthen these two.

sanskrit_shloka:
मनो नाम महाव्याघ्रो विषयारण्यभूमिषु ।
चरत्यत्र न गच्छन्तु साधवो ये मुमुक्षवः ॥ १७६ ॥
transliteration:
mano nāma mahāvyāghro viṣayāraṇyabhūmiṣu |
caratyatra na gacchantu sādhavo ye mumukṣavaḥ || 176 ||
translation: In the forest-tract of sense-pleasures there prowls a huge tiger called the mind. Let good people who have a longing for Liberation never go there.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the forest-tract of sense-pleasures there prowls a huge tiger called the mind. Let good people who have a longing for Liberation never go there.

sanskrit_shloka:
मनः प्रसूते विषयानशेषान् स्थूलात्मना सूक्ष्मतया च भोक्तुः ।
शरीरवर्णाश्रमजातिभेदान् गुणक्रियाहेतुफलानि नित्यम् ॥ १७७ ॥
transliteration:
manaḥ prasūte viṣayānaśeṣān sthūlātmanā sūkṣmatayā ca bhoktuḥ |
śarīravarṇāśramajātibhedān guṇakriyāhetuphalāni nityam || 177 ||
translation: The mind continually produces for the experiencer all sense-objects without exception, whether perceived as gross or fine, the differences of body, caste, order of life, and tribe, as well as the varieties of qualification, action, means and results.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The mind continually produces for the experiencer all sense-objects without exception, whether perceived as gross or fine, the differences of body, caste, order of life, and tribe, as well as the varieties of qualification, action, means and results.

sanskrit_shloka:
असङ्गचिद्रूपममुं विमोह्य देहेन्द्रियप्राणगुणैर्निबद्ध्य ।
अहंममेति भ्रमायात्यजस्रं मनः स्वकृत्येषु फलोपभुक्तिषु ॥ १७८ ॥
transliteration:
asaṅgacidrūpamamuṃ vimohya dehendriyaprāṇaguṇairnibaddhya |
ahaṃmameti bhraMāyātyajasraṃ manaḥ svakṛtyeṣu phalopabhuktiṣu || 178 ||
translation: Deluding the Jīva, which is unattached Pure Intelligence, and binding it by the ties of body, organs and Prāṇas, the mind causes it to wander, with ideas of 'I' and 'mine', amidst the varied enjoyment of results achieved by itself.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Deluding the Jīva, which is unattached Pure Intelligence, and binding it by the ties of body, organs and Prāṇas, the mind causes it to wander, with ideas of 'I' and 'mine', amidst the varied enjoyment of results achieved by itself.

sanskrit_shloka:
अध्यासदोषात्पुरुषस्य संसृतिः अध्यासबन्धस्त्वमुनैव कल्पितः ।
रजस्तमोदोषवतोऽविवेकिनो जन्मादिदुःखस्य निदानमेतत् ॥ १७९ ॥
transliteration:
adhyāsadoṣātpuruṣasya saṃsṛtiḥ adhyāsabandhastvamunaiva kalpitaḥ |
rajastamodoṣavato'vivekino janmādiduḥkhasya nidānametat || 179 ||
translation: Man’s transmigration is due to the evil of superimposition, and the bondage of superimposition is created by the mind alone. It is this that causes the misery of birth etc., for the man of non-discrimination who is tainted by Rajas and Tamas.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Man’s transmigration is due to the evil of superimposition, and the bondage of superimposition is created by the mind alone. It is this that causes the misery of birth etc., for the man of non-discrimination who is tainted by Rajas and Tamas.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतः प्राहुर्मनोऽविद्यां पण्डितास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ।
येनैव भ्राम्यते विश्वं वायुनेवाभ्रमण्डलम् ॥ १८0 ॥
transliteration:
ataḥ prāhurmano'vidyāṃ paṇḍitāstattvadarśinaḥ |
yenaiva bhrāmyate viśvaṃ vāyunevābhramaṇḍalam || 180 ||
translation: Hence sages who have fathomed its secret have designated the mind as Avidya or ignorance, by which alone the universe is moved to and fro, like masses of clouds by the wind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Hence sages who have fathomed its secret have designated the mind as Avidya or ignorance, by which alone the universe is moved to and fro, like masses of clouds by the wind.

sanskrit_shloka:
तन्मनःशोधनं कार्यं प्रयत्नेन मुमुक्षुणा ।
विशुद्धे सति चैतस्मिन्मुक्तिः करफलायते ॥ १८१ ॥
transliteration:
tanmanaḥśodhanaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnena mumukṣuṇā |
viśuddhe sati caitasminmuktiḥ karaphalāyate || 181 ||
translation: Therefore the seeker after Liberation must carefully purify the mind. When this is purified, Liberation is as easy of access as a fruit on the palm of one’s hand.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore the seeker after Liberation must carefully purify the mind. When this is purified, Liberation is as easy of access as a fruit on the palm of one’s hand.

sanskrit_shloka:
मोक्षैकसक्त्या विषयेषु रागं निर्मूल्य संन्यस्य च सर्वकर्म ।
सच्छ्रद्धया यः श्रवणादिनिष्ठो रजःस्वभावं स धुनोति बुद्धेः ॥ १८२ ॥
transliteration:
mokṣaikasaktyā viṣayeṣu rāgaṃ nirmūlya saṃnyasya ca sarvakarma |
sacchraddhayā yaḥ śravaṇādiniṣṭho rajaḥsvabhāvaṃ sa dhunoti buddheḥ || 182 ||
translation: He who by means of one-pointed devotion to Liberation roots out the attachment to sense-objects, renounces all actions, and with faith in the Real Brahman regularly practices hearing, etc., succeeds in purging the Rājasika nature of the intellect.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who by means of one-pointed devotion to Liberation roots out the attachment to sense-objects, renounces all actions, and with faith in the Real Brahman regularly practices hearing, etc., succeeds in purging the Rājasika nature of the intellect.

sanskrit_shloka:
मनोमयो नापि भवेत्परात्मा ह्याद्यन्तवत्त्वात्परिणामिभावात् ।
दुःखात्मकत्वाद्विषयत्वहेतोः द्रष्टा हि दृश्यात्मतया न दृष्टः ॥ १८३ ॥
transliteration:
manomayo nāpi bhavetparātmā hyādyantavattvātpariṇāmibhāvāt |
duḥkhātmakatvādviṣayatvahetoḥ draṣṭā hi dṛśyātmatayā na dṛṣṭaḥ || 183 ||
translation: Neither can the mental sheath be the Supreme Self, because it has a beginning and an end, is subject to modifications, is characterised by pain and suffering and is an object; whereas the subject can never be identified with the objects of knowledge.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Neither can the mental sheath be the Supreme Self, because it has a beginning and an end, is subject to modifications, is characterised by pain and suffering and is an object; whereas the subject can never be identified with the objects of knowledge.

sanskrit_shloka:
बुद्धिर्बुद्धीन्द्रियैः सार्धं सवृत्तिः कर्तृलक्षणः ।
विज्ञानमायाकोशः स्यात्पुंसः संसारकारणम् ॥ १८४ ॥
transliteration:
buddhirbuddhīndriyaiḥ sārdhaṃ savṛttiḥ kartṛlakṣaṇaḥ |
vijñānaMāyākośaḥ syātpuṃsaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam || 184 ||
translation: The Buddhi with its modifications and the organs of knowledge, forms the VijñānaMāyā Kośa or knowledge sheath, of the agent, having the characteristics which is the cause of man’s transmigration.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Buddhi with its modifications and the organs of knowledge, forms the VijñānaMāyā Kośa or knowledge sheath, of the agent, having the characteristics which is the cause of man’s transmigration.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनुव्रजच्चित्प्रतिबिम्बशक्तिः विज्ञानसंज्ञः प्रकृतेर्विकारः ।
ज्ञानक्रियावानहमित्यजस्रं देहेन्द्रियादिष्वभिमन्यते भृशम् ॥ १८५ ॥
transliteration:
anuvrajaccitpratibimbaśaktiḥ vijñānasaṃjñaḥ prakṛtervikāraḥ |
jñānakriyāvānahamityajasraṃ dehendriyādiṣvabhimanyate bhṛśam || 185 ||
translation: This knowledge sheath, which seems to be followed by a reflection of the power of the Chit, is a modification of the Prakriti, is endowed with the function of knowledge, and always wholly identifies itself with the body, organs, etc.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This knowledge sheath, which seems to be followed by a reflection of the power of the Chit, is a modification of the Prakriti, is endowed with the function of knowledge, and always wholly identifies itself with the body, organs, etc.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनादिकालोऽयमहंस्वभावो जीवः समस्तव्यवहारवोढा ।
करोति कर्माण्यपि पूर्ववासनः पुण्यान्यपुण्यानि च तत्फलानि ॥ १८६ ॥
transliteration:
भुङ्क्ते विचित्रास्वपि योनिषु व्रजन् नायाति निर्यात्यध ऊर्ध्वमेषः ।
अस्यैव विज्ञानमायास्य जाग्रत् स्वप्नाद्यवस्थाः सुखदुःखभोगः ॥ १८७ ॥
translation: 186-187. It is without beginning, characterised by egoism, is called the Jiva, and carries on all the activities on the relative plane. Through previous desires it performs good and evil actions and experiences their results. Being born in various bodies, it comes and goes, up and down. It is this knowledge sheath that has the waking, dream and other states, and experiences joy and grief.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 186-187. It is without beginning, characterised by egoism, is called the Jiva, and carries on all the activities on the relative plane. Through previous desires it performs good and evil actions and experiences their results. Being born in various bodies, it comes and goes, up and down. It is this knowledge sheath that has the waking, dream and other states, and experiences joy and grief.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहादिनिष्ठाश्रमधर्मकर्म गुणाभिमानः सततं ममेति ।
विज्ञानकोशोऽयमतिप्रकाशः प्रकृष्टसान्निध्यवशात्परात्मनः ।
अतो भवत्येष उपाधिरस्य यदात्मधीः संसरति भ्रमेण ॥ १८८ ॥
transliteration:
dehādiniṣṭhāśramadharmakarma guṇābhimānaḥ satataṃ mameti |
vijñānakośo'yamatiprakāśaḥ prakṛṣṭasānnidhyavaśātparātmanaḥ |
ato bhavatyeṣa upādhirasya yadātmadhīḥ saṃsarati bhrameṇa || 188 ||
translation: It always mistakes the duties, functions and attributes of the orders of life which belong to the body, as its own. The knowledge sheath is exceedingly effulgent, owing to its close proximity to the Supreme Self, which identifying Itself with it suffers transmigration through delusion. It is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It always mistakes the duties, functions and attributes of the orders of life which belong to the body, as its own. The knowledge sheath is exceedingly effulgent, owing to its close proximity to the Supreme Self, which identifying Itself with it suffers transmigration through delusion. It is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
देहादिनिष्ठाश्रमधर्मकर्म गुणाभिमानः सततं ममेति ।
विज्ञानकोशोऽयमतिप्रकाशः प्रकृष्टसान्निध्यवशात्परात्मनः ।
अतो भवत्येष उपाधिरस्य यदात्मधीः संसरति भ्रमेण ॥ १८८ ॥
transliteration:
dehādiniṣṭhāśramadharmakarma guṇābhimānaḥ satataṃ mameti |
vijñānakośo'yamatiprakāśaḥ prakṛṣṭasānnidhyavaśātparātmanaḥ |
ato bhavatyeṣa upādhirasya yadātmadhīḥ saṃsarati bhrameṇa || 188 ||
translation: It always mistakes the duties, functions and attributes of the orders of life which belong to the body, as its own. The knowledge sheath is exceedingly effulgent, owing to its close proximity to the Supreme Self, which identifying Itself with it suffers transmigration through delusion. It is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It always mistakes the duties, functions and attributes of the orders of life which belong to the body, as its own. The knowledge sheath is exceedingly effulgent, owing to its close proximity to the Supreme Self, which identifying Itself with it suffers transmigration through delusion. It is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
योऽयं विज्ञानमायाः प्राणेषु हृदि स्फुरत्ययं ज्योतिः ।
कूटस्थः सन्नात्मा कर्ता भोक्ता भवत्युपाधिस्थः ॥ १८९ ॥
transliteration:
yo'yaṃ vijñānaMāyāḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdi sphuratyayaṃ jyotiḥ |
kūṭasthaḥ sannātmā kartā bhoktā bhavatyupādhisthaḥ || 189 ||
translation: The self-effulgent Ātman, which is Pure Knowledge, shines in the midst of the Prāṇas, within the heart. Though immutable, It becomes the agent and experiencer owing to Its superimposition, the knowledge sheath.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The self-effulgent Ātman, which is Pure Knowledge, shines in the midst of the Prāṇas, within the heart. Though immutable, It becomes the agent and experiencer owing to Its superimposition, the knowledge sheath.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वयं परिच्छेदमुपेत्य बुद्धेः तादात्म्यदोषेण परं मृषात्मनः ।
सर्वात्मकः सन्नपि वीक्षते स्वयं स्वतः पृथक्त्वेन मृदो घटानिव ॥ १९0 ॥
transliteration:
svayaṃ paricchedamupetya buddheḥ tādātmyadoṣeṇa paraṃ mṛṣātmanaḥ |
sarvātmakaḥ sannapi vīkṣate svayaṃ svataḥ pṛthaktvena mṛdo ghaṭāniva || 190 ||
translation: Though the Self of everything that exists, this Ātman, Itself assuming the limitations of the Buddhi and wrongly identifying Itself with this totally unreal entity, looks upon Itself as something different – like earthen jars from the clay of which they are made.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Though the Self of everything that exists, this Ātman, Itself assuming the limitations of the Buddhi and wrongly identifying Itself with this totally unreal entity, looks upon Itself as something different – like earthen jars from the clay of which they are made.

sanskrit_shloka:
उपाधिसंबन्धवशात्परात्मा ह्युपाधिधर्माननुभाति तद्गुणः ।
अयोविकारानविकारिवन्हिवत् सदैकरूपोऽपि परः स्वभावात् ॥ १९१ ॥
transliteration:
upādhisaṃbandhavaśātparātmā hyupādhidharmānanubhāti tadguṇaḥ |
ayovikārānavikārivanhivat sadaikarūpo'pi paraḥ svabhāvāt || 191 ||
translation: Owing to Its connection with the super-impositions, the Supreme Self, even thou naturally perfect (transcending Nature) and eternally unchanging, assumes the qualities of the superimpositions and appears to act just as they do – like the changeless fire assuming the modifications of the iron which it turns red-hot.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Owing to Its connection with the super-impositions, the Supreme Self, even thou naturally perfect (transcending Nature) and eternally unchanging, assumes the qualities of the superimpositions and appears to act just as they do – like the changeless fire assuming the modifications of the iron which it turns red-hot.

sanskrit_shloka:
शिष्य उवाच भ्रमेणाप्यन्यथा वास्तु जीवभावः परात्मनः ।
तदुपाधेरनादित्वान्नानादेर्नाश इष्यते ॥ १९२ ॥
transliteration:
śiṣya uvāca bhrameṇāpyanyathā vāstu jīvabhāvaḥ parātmanaḥ |
tadupādheranāditvānnānādernāśa iṣyate || 192 ||
translation: The disciple questioned: Be it through delusion or otherwise that the Supreme Self has come to consider Itself as the Jīva, this superimposition is without beginning, and that which has no beginning cannot be supposed to have an end either.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The disciple questioned: Be it through delusion or otherwise that the Supreme Self has come to consider Itself as the Jīva, this superimposition is without beginning, and that which has no beginning cannot be supposed to have an end either.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतोऽस्य जीवभावोऽपि नित्या भवति संसृतिः ।
न निवर्तेत तन्मोक्षः कथं मे श्रीगुरो वद ॥ १९३ ॥
transliteration:
ato'sya jīvabhāvo'pi nityā bhavati saṃsṛtiḥ |
na nivarteta tanmokṣaḥ kathaṃ me śrīguro vada || 193 ||
translation: Therefore the Jīvahood of the soul also must have no end, and its transmigration must continue for ever. How then can there be Liberation for the soul? Kindly enlighten me on this point, O revered Master.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore the Jīvahood of the soul also must have no end, and its transmigration must continue for ever. How then can there be Liberation for the soul? Kindly enlighten me on this point, O revered Master.

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रीगुरुरुवाच सम्यक्पृष्टं त्वया विद्वन्सावधानेन तच्छृणु ।
प्रामाणिकी न भवति भ्रान्त्या मोहितकल्पना ॥ १९४ ॥
transliteration:
śrīgururuvāca samyakpṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vidvansāvadhānena tacchṛṇu |
prāmāṇikī na bhavati bhrāntyā mohitakalpanā || 194 ||
translation: The Teacher said: Thou hast rightly questioned, O learned man! Listen therefore attentively: The imagination which has been conjured up by delusion can never be accepted as a fact.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Teacher said: Thou hast rightly questioned, O learned man! Listen therefore attentively: The imagination which has been conjured up by delusion can never be accepted as a fact.

sanskrit_shloka:
भ्रान्तिं विना त्वसङ्गस्य निष्क्रियस्य निराकृतेः ।
न घटेतार्थसंबन्धो नभसो नीलतादिवत् ॥ १९५ ॥
transliteration:
bhrāntiṃ vinā tvasaṅgasya niṣkriyasya nirākṛteḥ |
na ghaṭetārthasaṃbandho nabhaso nīlatādivat || 195 ||
translation: But for delusion there can be no connection of the Self – which is unattached, beyond activity and formless – with the objective world, as in the case of blueness etc., with reference to the sky.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: But for delusion there can be no connection of the Self – which is unattached, beyond activity and formless – with the objective world, as in the case of blueness etc., with reference to the sky.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वस्य द्रष्टुर्निर्गुणस्याक्रियस्य प्रत्यग्बोधानन्दरूपस्य बुद्धेः ।
भ्रान्त्या प्राप्तो जीवभावो न सत्यो मोहापाये नास्त्यवस्तुस्वभावात् ॥ १९६ ॥
transliteration:
svasya draṣṭurnirguṇasyākriyasya pratyagbodhānandarūpasya buddheḥ |
bhrāntyā prāpto jīvabhāvo na satyo mohāpāye nāstyavastusvabhāvāt || 196 ||
translation: The Jīvahood of the Ātman, the Witness, which is beyond qualities and beyond activity, and which is realised within as Knowledge and Bliss Absolute – has been superimposed by the delusion of the Buddhi, and is not real. And because it is by nature an unreality, it ceases to exist when the delusion is gone.

sanskrit_shloka:
यावद्भ्रान्तिस्तावदेवास्य सत्ता मिथ्याज्ञानोज्जृम्भितस्य प्रमादात् ।
रज्ज्वां सर्पो भ्रान्तिकालीन एव भ्रान्तेर्नाशे नैव सर्पोऽपि तद्वत् ॥ १९७ ॥
transliteration:
yāvadbhrāntistāvadevāsya sattā mithyājñānojjṛmbhitasya pramādāt |
rajjvāṃ sarpo bhrāntikālīna eva bhrānternāśe naiva sarpo'pi tadvat || 197 ||
translation: It exists only so long as the delusion lasts, being caused by indiscrimination due to an illusion. The rope is supposed to be the snake only so long as the mistake lasts, and there is no more snake when the illusion has vanished. Similar is the case here.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनादित्वमविद्यायाः कार्यस्यापि तथेष्यते ।
उत्पन्नायां तु विद्यायामाविद्यकमनाद्यपि ॥ १९८ ॥
transliteration:
प्रबोधे स्वप्नवत्सर्वं सहमूलं विनश्यति ।
अनाद्यपीदं नो नित्यं प्रागभाव इव स्फुटम् ॥ १९९ ॥
translation: 198-199. Avidya or Nescience and its effects are likewise considered as beginningless. But with the rise of Vidyā or realisation, the entire effects of Avidya, even though beginningless, are destroyed together with their root – like dreams on waking up from sleep. It is clear that the phenomenal universe, even though without beginning, is not eternal – like previous non-existence.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनादेरपि विध्वंसः प्रागभावस्य वीक्षितः ।
यद्बुद्ध्युपाधिसंबन्धात्परिकल्पितमात्मनि ॥ २00 ॥
transliteration:
जीवत्वं न ततोऽन्यस्तु स्वरूपेण विलक्षणः ।
संबन्धस्त्वात्मनो बुद्ध्या मिथ्याज्ञानपुरःसरः ॥ २0१ ॥
translation: 200-201. Previous non-existence, even though beginningless, is observed to have an end. So the Jīvahood which is imagined to be in the Ātman through its relation with superimposed attributes such as the Buddhi, is not real; whereas the other (the Ātman) is essentially different from it. The relation between the Ātman and the Buddhi is due to a false knowledge.

sanskrit_shloka:
विनिवृत्तिर्भवेत्तस्य सम्यग्ज्ञानेन नान्यथा ।
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वविज्ञानं सम्यग्ज्ञानं श्रुतेर्मतम् ॥ २0२ ॥
transliteration:
vinivṛttirbhavettasya samyagjñānena nānyathā |
brahmātmaikatvavijñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ śrutermatam || 202 ||
translation: The cessation of that superimposition takes place through perfect knowledge, and by no other means. Perfect knowledge, according to the Śrutis, consists in the realisation of the identity of the individual soul and Brahman.
